body:
Having this in `typedefs.h` can break code elsewhere that would do:
```
#ifdef __has_feature
#if __has_feature(foo)
// Do stuff.
#endif
#else
#if defined(__FOO__)
// Do stuff.
#endif
#endif
```
as it wouldn't run the `#else`.

That's a bit convoluted but I wouldn't be surprised to find code like this in thirdparty libs (not affected by our typedefs for the most part) but still it's a bad practice IMO as `#ifdef __has_feature` is a very common check before using `__has_feature`.

body:
It's not too big a deal as it only impacts sanitizers-enabled builds, but isn't this going contrary to the aim to reduce transitive includes in the codebase?

This will force include these interfaces in pretty much every single Godot file, while it seems before that it was only needed in `rid_owner.h` and a couple of tests.

Yeah, I've since learned just how much certain implementations *explicitly* rely on an undefined `__has_feature` versus it simply returning false. To keep one-liner convenience and retain compatibility, this could be changed to:
```cpp
#ifdef __has_feature
#define GD_HAS_FEATURE(m_name) __has_feature(m_name)
#else
#define GD_HAS_FEATURE(m_name) 0
#endif // __has_feature
```

On paper, it'd absolutely be better to do that. However, we don't have the most uniform means of enabling/handling sanitizer logic at the moment. I'd feel better about doing that in a context where sanitizers are recognized/toggleable on a per-compiler basis, rather than a per-platform basis (though this is a broader issue). I'll absolutely look into incorporating that in an alternative PR though, get a feel for how tedious it'd be

With that said, I can most likely incorporate this into the buildsystem as-is. Will try that out now
